title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Reverse
summary: Given a string s of lowercase English letters, you can reverse either the first k characters or the last k characters for any k from 1 to n.
statement: Given a string s of lowercase English letters, you can reverse either the first k characters or the last k characters for any k from 1 to n. Perform exactly one such operation to achieve the lexicographically smallest possible string.
constraints: s contains one to 1,000 lowercase letters.
Perform exactly one operation: reverse a prefix or a suffix of any length from one through n.
Return the lexicographically smallest obtainable string.
hints: There are only two allowed operations for each length.
Enumerate every prefix reversal and every suffix reversal and retain the smallest result.
Include length one and the full string; length one also represents a no-visible-change legal operation.
The enumeration contains every permitted single operation exactly by its side and length, so its minimum is optimal.
editorial: The enumeration contains every permitted single operation exactly by its side and length, so its minimum is optimal.

tests.explanation: Reversing the first three characters changes dca to acd and produces acdb.
Reversing the final three characters produces aabb.
